In [[mathematical cryptography]], a '''Kleinian integer''' is a [[complex number]] of the form <math>m+n\frac{1+\sqrt{-7}}{2}</math>, with ''m'' and ''n'' [[Integer|rational integers]]. They are named after [[Felix Klein]].

The Kleinian integers form a [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] called the '''Kleinian ring''', which is the [[ring of integers]] in the imaginary [[quadratic field]] <math>\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7})</math>. This ring is a [[unique factorization domain]].
